title: Research Science Institute (RSI) 2027
summary: Research Science Institute is a free six-week summer research program at MIT and Stanford for high school juniors. Participants complete STEM coursework and individual research projects guided by experienced mentors.

judging.name: Academic Achievement and Test Scores
judging.detail: Demonstrated superior scholastic achievement in mathematics and science, supported by coursework and standardized test scores (e.g., PSAT Math 740+, SAT Math 750+, ACT Math 33+).

evidence.quote: RSI students typically demonstrate superior academic achievement in math and science and a genuine passion for research.
evidence.context: RSI students are selected based on their potential as future leaders in STEM. RSI students typically demonstrate superior academic achievement in math and science and a genuine passion for research. RSI students have taken rigorous STEM courses and participated in extracurricular activities like science competitions or independent research projects.

judging.name: STEM Passion and Independent Inquiry
judging.detail: Curiosity, self-motivated learning, and interest in scientific research demonstrated through essays and extracurricular projects.

evidence.quote: Demonstrate your curiosity and passion for a subject through your essays.
evidence.context: Demonstrate your curiosity and passion for a subject through your essays. Write about a specific topic that fascinates you, a challenging problem you have tried to solve, or a time you went beyond your school curriculum to learn something new. Show do not just tell: Give concrete examples of your self-motivated learning. For instance, describe a personal project you undertook, a difficult book you read, or an online course you completed that is related to your scientific interests. You can write about your participation in a school science or math club, a science fair, or even a part-time job.

judging.name: Leadership and Extracurricular Activities
judging.detail: Leadership potential demonstrated through STEM activities, competitions, independent projects, and community contributions.

flags.explanation: International applicants cannot apply directly on their own unless their country has an active sponsorship agreement and designated selection procedure with CEE.

evidence.quote: RSI will accept international students. The specific countries depend on the sponsors working with CEE.
evidence.context: RSI will accept international students. The specific countries depend on the sponsors working with CEE. If you are an international student, please contact Maite Ballestero, Executive VP of Programs, and she can let you know which countries are likely to sponsor students this year. The deadline for applications from international students is the same as for U.S. students unless there is a different process for a particular country.
